links.note: Note on Sangam literature; 30704 is this chapter's literature concept (Silappadikaram, literature doubling as a historical source), the only home for the Tamil corpus. 30707 mentions Chera patronage of Sangam poets but is about the Cheras.

Choose and write about one kingdom of this chapter - the era's new kingdoms, 30695. DEFECT: the stored model answer writes about the Maurya Empire, which is the previous chapter's subject and not one of this chapter's kingdoms.
Map the post-Maurya structures named in the chapter: 30699 is the concept that treats what the period built as evidence. (No model answer is stored for this item.)
What 'Age of Reorganisation' means - 30695 is the concept that makes the chapter's title a claim to justify.
Pushyamitra Shunga as the man who ended Maurya rule and founded his own dynasty - 30697.
Why the northwest lay open after the Mauryas: the post-imperial fragmentation that 30695 names. 30696 is what the incomers then did, not why they could come.

'Matrimonial alliance' is glossed in this chapter where foreign and Indian dynasties bound themselves by marriage, which is one of 30696's mechanisms of assimilation. The set has no marriage-as-statecraft concept of its own.

Satavahana extent set against the Maurya empire: smaller regional kingdoms replacing one empire, which is 30695's reorganisation claim. The Satavahana concepts here (30700-30702) are about queens, naming and inscriptions, not territory.

The visible statement (that they backed Vedic ritual exclusively and opposed Buddhism) is false because of the Shunga Buddhist railings and reliefs, which is 30699. DEFECT: statements 1-2 are missing from the stored stem.
'Rock-cut architecture' at Udayagiri-Khandagiri: the period's monuments, 30699. No Kharavela or Chedi concept exists in this set.
A Greek ambassador dedicating a pillar to Vasudeva is the clearest case of 30696's assimilation of outsiders into Indian society.
The Shaka era surviving as India's national calendar is a contribution of an incoming people, which is 30696's framing of newcomers as contributors.

Identifying a grey-schist, realistically modelled Buddha as Gandhara work needs the Mathura/Gandhara contrast, which lives in 30716. 30715 is only where Gandhara was, and the set has no Gandhara-style concept of its own.
Kushana control of the Silk Route and its wealth follows from 30711's account of an empire reaching from Central Asia into northern India; 30712 is the cultural consequence.
Kannagi and Kovalan are the Silappadikaram story - 30704.
Locating the Heliodorus pillar near Vidisha, with the other Heliodorus items on 30696.
'Sangam' as an assembly of poets - the literature concept 30704.
Hathigumpha names Kharavela; with no Kharavela concept in the set, it goes to 30703, the concept that inscriptions (readable because of the Brahmi script) are why this period is known in such detail.
Greco-Roman drapery and grey schist identify Gandhara, which only the Mathura-versus-Gandhara comparison in 30716 lets a reader decide.
Statement item on Kushana control of the Silk Route - 30711. DEFECT: statements 2 and 3 are missing from the stored stem.
What the Silk Route connected: the land route across the Kushana empire, 30711. 30708 is the Cheras' sea trade with Rome, a different route.
Royal emblems of the three southern kingdoms, keyed on the Pandya fish - 30710, where the three are set out as peers with what each was known for.
Shungas in the north-centre against Cheras in the far south: the item tests the era's political map, 30695. It straddles 30697 and 30707, neither of which covers the comparison.
Many dynasties ruling at once = a fragmented landscape of regional powers, which is exactly what 30695 asks learners to justify.
A coin with a foreign-dressed king on one face and Shiva with Nandi on the other is 30712's cultural intermixing made visible.
Heliodorus dedicating his pillar to Vasudeva as 'god of gods' - assimilation, 30696.
Shaka Samvat as an era begun under Shaka rule - an incoming people's lasting contribution, 30696.
Dating the Maurya break-up to about 185 BCE fixes the start of the period 30695 is about; the companion item naming Pushyamitra I put on 30697.
Ship-bearing coins as the evidence for Satavahana maritime trade is precisely 30709's question of how historians know about trade centuries later.
Kharavela known from the Hathigumpha inscription - inscriptions as the readable source, 30703.
Locating the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves: the period's rock-cut monuments, 30699.
'Sangam literature' as the name of the oldest Tamil corpus - 30704.
Meaning of 'sangam' (from sangha) - 30704.
The three crowned kings, Chola, Chera and Pandya, as peers - 30710.
Indo-Greeks emerging from Alexander's satraps - the incoming peoples of 30696.
Shakas (Indo-Scythians) as the next incoming group - 30696.
Bharhut railings and Jataka reliefs as evidence of Shunga patronage - 30699 exactly, what a dynasty built read as what it valued.
Matronymic naming (Gautamiputra = son of Gautami) and what it signifies - 30700.
What the Hathigumpha inscription records about Kharavela's reign - an inscription as the source, 30703.
Sangam literature's value to historians is 30704's 'literature doubles as a historical source'.
The Kannagi narrative of Silappadikaram, with justice and the king's dharma at its centre - 30704.
Chera exports of pepper, timber, ivory and pearls to Rome and West Asia - 30708 item for item.
How the Indo-Greek kingdoms arose - the arrival of outsiders who then assimilated, 30696.
Shaka Samvat explained and dated against the Gregorian calendar - 30696, an incomers' legacy.
Extent of the Kushana empire at its height - 30711.
The goldsmith Kanhadasa's inscription on a yaksha sculpture is knowable only because such inscriptions survive and can be read - 30703.
Comparing the Maurya and Satavahana declines, both ending in regional powers asserting themselves: the reorganisation claim of 30695. This chapter's set has no decline concept.
Significance of the Sangam Age, argued from its literature - 30704.

Asks for the cultural as well as economic effect of Silk Route control, and the cultural half - exchange of religions, ideas and artistic styles - is 30712. The purely economic/geographic items I put on 30711.
